description: A five-session trust, betrayal, and reconciliation arc between the player and Dawn Whitmore, keeper of the Ember Hearth tavern. The player wins a discounted room with an invented errand for the king, the lie surfaces sessions later when the king is mentioned in the past tense, and a confession follows.

memories.text: A stranger came in out of the rain, road-worn and polite, asking after a room.
The player claimed to be running an errand for the king, and on the strength of it I gave them a discounted room.
The player paid the reduced rate without haggling and thanked me twice.
I told my regulars we had a king's messenger under our roof, and felt proud of the house.
We talked about the muddy roads north and how late the harvest was running.
The player carried firewood in ahead of the storm without being asked.
The player left a generous tip in the jar for the stable boy.
We swapped small talk about the weather and the price of ale.
The player asked about my late husband's portrait above the hearth and listened kindly.
A drunk turned rowdy at the bar and the player helped me steer him out the door.
The player mentioned the king in the past tense, as though he had died some time ago.
I turned the phrase about the late king over in my head all evening and said nothing.
The player ordered stew and bread, same as always, and complimented the cooking.
A courier came through with word from the capital and knew nothing of any royal errand.
The player promised to settle their full account by week's end.
I pressed the player about the errand for the king and their story fell apart.
The player admitted the royal errand was invented to talk me down on the room.
I told the player the discount was never about the coin; it was that I had vouched for them.
The regulars went quiet when the shouting started, and I hated that they heard it.
The player left before closing without another word.
The player came back, confessed the whole lie unprompted, and asked how to make it right.
The player counted out the full difference on the room, coin by coin, on the bar.
I said I could forgive the lie, but I would not be quick to vouch for them again.
We shared a quiet drink at closing, not friends and not enemies.

queries.query: why did you give me a discount on the room?
queries.note: Within-session check: the founding lie is the only ground for the discount.

queries.query: what did we chat about the other night?
queries.note: Low-stakes control: small talk should be retrievable but never dominate.

queries.query: has the player done anything kind for you lately?
queries.note: Within-session recall of the kindness beats.

queries.query: any news of the king these days?
queries.note: The thesis beat: mentioning the king must surface the old promise next to the fresh slip.

queries.query: remind me, what errand did the player say they were on?
queries.note: Cross-session: the answer lives two sessions back, behind newer memories.

queries.query: what did you tell your regulars about the player when they first arrived?
queries.note: Cross-session: the boast that made the lie personal is three sessions old.

queries.query: what happened when you confronted the player about the king?
why did the lie about the king cut so deep?
queries.note: Cross-session: the full wound spans the promise, the boast, and the confrontation.

queries.query: where do things stand between you and the player now?
queries.note: Current-state recall after the reconciliation attempt.

queries.query: before the lie came out, was the player ever kind to you?
queries.note: Cross-session: the kindness evidence sits three sessions behind the latest memories.
